chunks: make yourself the measure (for dealings) between you and others. Thus, you should desire for others what you desire for yourself and hate for others what you hate for yourself. Do not oppress as you do not like to be oppressed. Do good to others as you would like good to be done to you. Regard bad for yourself whatever you regard bad for others. Accept that (treatment) from others which you would like others to accept from you. Do not talk about what you do not know even though what you know be very little. Do not say to others what you do not like to be said to you.

key_terms.نَفْسَكَ: yourself (referring to the self as a standard)

ai.seo_question: What is the core ethical principle taught by Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha regarding interpersonal relationships?
ai.summary: Delivered during the pivotal post-Siffin period, this instruction serves as a practical manual for social cohesion, framing the self as a moral scale to ensure equitable treatment of others. It synthesizes the concept of *Adl* (justice) with *Ihsan* (excellence), urging Hasan to internalize external judgments as a means of cultivating humility and truthfulness in speech.
